purpose: Separate two GBIF-indexed Philippine market vouchers for Mugil cephalus from a distinct historical Cagayan River study report; assess what each source can support for the B0380 basin candidate.

basin.name: Cagayan
basin.meaning: Northern Luzon Cagayan drainage candidate; not Cagayan de Misamis in Mindanao and not a precise river-reach geometry.

taxon.taxonomicCaveat: The 2009 northwest-Pacific phylogeography paper describes strongly divergent geographic lineages and says global taxonomic status needs further study. This review keeps the source name and assigns no lineage or replacement species name.

findings.sourceType: 2017 conference paper; full text reviewed from an author-uploaded ResearchGate copy; conference-paper citation also appears in an NFRDI journal article bibliography.

collectionSiteTable.coordinateLimit: The coordinate is a study-site value. The paper gives no datum, coordinate uncertainty, or voucher-specific capture point; it is not used here as exact specimen geometry.

findings.voucherLimit: The paper says representative specimens were preserved as vouchers, and its table associates three Cagayan codes with the taxon. It does not name a public repository or provide institutional catalog numbers that were independently checked.
findings.methodLimit: The general methods describe seine-net collections at thirteen sites and complementary fish-market surveys. The species account says this taxon was collected in Cagayan River, but the method is not itemized per voucher code.
findings.sequenceInterpretation: The table and discussion associate the Cagayan samples with an exact-match COI comparison to GenBank accession JQ060553, isolate 358. The conference paper calls that comparator a Pearl River sequence 'in Taiwan'; a 2020 UFAL doctoral-thesis sequence table maps JQ060553 / isolate 358 to Pearl River, China. The NCBI accession page was not directly retrieved, so the locality mismatch remains an accession-level follow-up. No separate public sequence accession linked to Phil-CAG1–3 was verified; the comparator is not treated as a Cagayan specimen record.
findings.basinInterpretation: This is a direct historical, basin-scale Cagayan River report and materially strengthens the B0380 discovery candidate beyond the market vouchers. It does not establish current presence, abundance, an exact station/reach, or public-app-ready geometry.

findings.sourceType: Two distinct NMNH voucher catalog numbers exposed through GBIF occurrence/material-sample feeds; the six indexed rows are duplicate feed representations, not six independent capture records.

specimens.sourceLocality: Smithsonian metadata says purchased at Santa Teresita market; vendor stated capture was in the vicinity of Santa Teresita, Cagayan Province, Luzon.
specimens.interpretation: The polygon hit is for the published coordinate, while the specimen was a market purchase and the vendor-reported catch vicinity was not independently verified as a capture station.

specimens.sourceLocality: FDA confirms the voucher is from the Philippines 2012 NMNH market survey. No exact capture locality was verified in this review.
specimens.interpretation: A GBIF coordinate and market-survey voucher do not identify the fish's capture point or establish a Cagayan-basin catch locality.

findings.overallInterpretation: Neither market coordinate is used as an exact catch point. The 405775 vendor vicinity is a separate, less precise lead; it is not merged with the Cagayan River conference-study samples.

disposition.historicalCagayanRiverAssociation: Supported by one conference-paper report with three study voucher codes, date, and a site coordinate; independent museum re-examination and voucher-repository linkage remain outstanding.
disposition.reason: The conference report is a meaningful historical basin-level lead but its voucher repository and item-level reuse rights are unresolved, its site coordinate is not specimen-point precision, and the cited GenBank comparator is not a local sample accession. Market records report purchases and vendor vicinity rather than verified capture points.

sources.supports: Author-uploaded conference-paper full text: named Cagayan River report, Cagayan/Camalaniugan site, coordinate, collection date, voucher codes, methods, and the JQ060553 comparator wording.
Independent bibliographic citation of the 2017 item as a conference paper; not a second verification of its sample data.
Jamandre et al. (2009): Pearl River is in southern China; Luzon samples were estuarine; the paper discusses divergent geographic lineages and unresolved species limits.

Neves (2020) doctoral-thesis Table S4.2 independently cross-references JQ060553 to Mugil cephalus isolate 358 from Pearl River, China; this is a secondary accession crosswalk, not evidence about the Cagayan sample.
